headline: mat-diffusion-analysis: diffusivity and activation energy from MD
claim: An AtomisticSkills skill that reads ASE trajectories at several temperatures, takes the diffusivity from the mean squared displacement and fits a weighted Arrhenius line for E_a.

hero.title: MSD slope to Arrhenius slope
hero.text: analyze_diffusion.py runs pymatgen's DiffusionAnalyzer on each trajectory after a 5 ps equilibration skip and reports D with its error. calculate_activation_energy.py fits ln D against 1/T, weighted by those errors.

features.title: Several temperatures
features.text: The skill asks for NVT or NPT runs at 4 to 6 temperatures between 600 and 1200 K from the run_md tool of the mace or matgl skill, in supercells over 10 A on every side.

features.title: Early stopping
features.text: The diffusion monitor stops a run once the transport property has converged and writes diffusion_{specie}.json and the MSD plot into the trajectory folder.

features.title: Weighted fit with uncertainties
features.text: The fit weights each temperature by the standard deviation of its D. The covariance propagates into E_a and into the conductivity extrapolated to 300 K in mS/cm.

features.title: Inputs and outputs
features.text: Input is an ASE .traj file per temperature with its .log for the frame interval. Outputs are diffusion_results.json per run, msd_{specie}.png and arrhenius_plot.png.

workflow.title: Run MD
workflow.text: run_md at 4 to 6 temperatures, supercell_min_length 10 A, diffusion monitor optional.

workflow.title: Arrhenius fit
workflow.text: calculate_activation_energy.py results/ reads md_*K/diffusion_results.json and fits E_a.

workflow.title: Check linearity
workflow.text: Inspect the MSD plots for a linear regime and the R^2 of the Arrhenius line.

applications.title: Li in Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS)
applications.text: A 2x2x1 supercell of about 200 atoms, 20 ps of NVT at 600 to 1000 K with MatPES-r2SCAN, gives E_a = 0.152 +/- 0.035 eV and a 300 K conductivity of 91.44 +/- 79.18 mS/cm.

detail.heading: Einstein diffusivity and a weighted Arrhenius fit
detail.text: analyze_diffusion.py converts the ASE frames after the ignore_ps skip into pymatgen structures and calls DiffusionAnalyzer.from_structures with smoothed=False and step_skip=1, using the frame interval read from the MD .log file. The diffusivity of the chosen species comes from the slope of the mean squared displacement, in cm^2/s, with its standard deviation from the structural variance of the MSD. calculate_activation_energy.py collects md_*K/diffusion_results.json and calls pymatgen's fit_arrhenius with the per-temperature errors. It fits the Arrhenius law D(T) = D0 exp(-E_a/k_B T) as a weighted line in ln D against 1/T.

detail.heading: Numerics and checks
detail.text: The SKILL.md asks for 4 to 6 temperatures, typically between 600 and 1200 K, supercells longer than 10 A in every direction and more than 20 mobile ions for the statistics. The user should check the MSD for a linear regime after the equilibration skip, 5.0 ps by default. The fitting script prints R^2 and warns below 0.95. It propagates the uncertainties through the covariance matrix of the weighted fit into E_a and into the diffusivity and ionic conductivity extrapolated to 300 K through pymatgen's get_extrapolated_conductivity, which takes the structure file given by --structure. In the LGPS example this gives 0.152 +/- 0.035 eV and 91.44 +/- 79.18 mS/cm from five 20 ps runs.

detail.heading: Interfaces and environment
detail.text: Trajectories must be ASE .traj files, produced by the run_md tool of a potential skill such as mace or matgl, which expands the cell to supercell_min_length (10 A by default) and can run several structures at once. The diffusion monitor from mat-md-monitors stops a run when D has converged within a threshold and saves diffusion_{specie}.json and msd_{specie}.png itself, so step 2 is skipped for those runs. The analysis scripts run in the cpu environment through venv/run. The sibling skill mat-md-monitors documents the monitors.
